data.description:
## Problem

The Jira API-token outage took the Reconcile Bridge down and produced **zero CloudWatch
signal**. The bridge runs on GitHub Actions, not on the monitored host, so nothing in
`infra/scripts/observability.sh` (the host probe that publishes every `rebar/host` metric) can
see it. Its only failure surface today is `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:264-279`
("Notify on bridge failure"), which writes a step summary and an `::error` annotation — visible
only to someone already looking at the run. GitHub Actions *can* publish to CloudWatch; nothing
in this repo does it yet.

## Design

**(a) Publish the metric from the workflow.** Add to the `reconcile` job in
`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`:

- `id-token: write` at **job** level (the workflow-level block at :58-60 is `contents: write` +
  `actions: write`; job-level is where `structured-output-baseline.yml:39-41` puts it for the
  same reason).
- an OIDC credential step mirroring `structured-output-baseline.yml:60-67`
  (`aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6`, `role-to-assume` + `aws-region` from repo
  `vars`), gated on `always()` so it is present on both the success and failure paths, and on
  the canonical repo + the var being set so forks and unconfigured checkouts skip it.
- `bridge_run_failures = 1` on `if: failure()`, and `= 0` on `if: success()`, both
  `aws cloudwatch put-metric-data --namespace rebar/host --metric-name bridge_run_failures
  --unit Count --value <n>`, dimensionless on both sides (`monitoring_s4b.tf`: a dimension on
  only one side silently unmatches the alarm).

*Why publish 0 on success rather than relying on missing-data semantics:* with
`treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"` a failure-only metric would alarm correctly, but the
metric would be absent whenever things are healthy — indistinguishable from "the publisher
itself is broken/unauthorized", and the alarm would sit in `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` rather than `OK`.
The success-path 0 makes the *publisher* continuously observable, matching the existing host
probe, which publishes `gerrit_healthy`/`reviewbot_healthy` as 0-or-1 every tick rather than
only on failure (`observability.sh:45-51`). Telemetry steps are `continue-on-error` so a
metric publish can never fail an otherwise-converged reconcile pass.

**(b) IAM.** Do **not** widen `rebar-terraform-plan` (`iam.tf:144-199`, `ReadOnlyAccess` +
`kms:Decrypt` — it is the drift-detection role and single-owner) and do not widen the Bedrock CI
role. Add a **new** narrowly-scoped role in `infra/terraform`, reusing the repo's existing OIDC
pattern: trust `aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.github` (`oidc.tf:14`) with the same
`aud = sts.amazonaws.com` + `sub` StringLike `repo:navapbc/rebar:*` conditions, and one inline
policy granting **only** `cloudwatch:PutMetricData`, constrained by the standard
`cloudwatch:namespace` StringEquals condition to `rebar/host`. PutMetricData takes no resource
ARN, so the namespace condition is what makes it narrow.

**(c) Alarm.** A new CloudWatch alarm on `rebar/host:bridge_run_failures`, styled on the
`rebar-autodeploy-*` alarms (`monitoring_autodeploy.tf:113-150`): `Sum`, dimensionless,
`treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"`, SNS `alarm_actions` + `ok_actions`, description naming
the runbook action (open the workflow run; check Jira token validity). Cadence differs
deliberately from the autodeploy 900s/threshold-0: the bridge runs every ~20 min, so a single
failed pass is routinely a transient network/API blip, while the token outage was sustained.
`period = 3600` with `threshold = 1` / `GreaterThanThreshold` alarms on the **second** failed
pass within an hour — a flake stays quiet, a real outage pages within ~40 minutes.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `reconcile-bridge.yml` publishes `rebar/host:bridge_run_failures` = 1 on failure and 0 on
   success, authenticated by OIDC via repo `vars` and skipped outside the canonical repo;
   `actionlint` and `zizmor` pass on the edited workflow.
2. A new IAM role in `infra/terraform` grants exactly `cloudwatch:PutMetricData` conditioned on
   `cloudwatch:namespace = rebar/host`, federating the existing GitHub OIDC provider; no
   existing role's permissions are widened.
3. A `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` on the new metric exists with
   `treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"` and a description naming the runbook action;
   `terraform fmt -check` + `terraform validate` pass (mind the 1024-char
   `alarm_description` cap).
4. Change lands on `main` through Gerrit with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.
5. The operator has run `terraform apply` for the new role + alarm, and the alarm exists in
   CloudWatch. (Apply is operator-run; this ticket stays open until it is confirmed.)
data.title: Publish bridge run failures to CloudWatch and alarm
